Extracted requirements from B.3.2 Forwarding Buffer (spec/appendix-bufferbloat.md lines 124-135):

The spec uses implementation-guidance style (lowercase "must") rather than RFC 2119 normative language (uppercase MUST/SHALL). Translated requirements:

## Forwarding Buffer Requirements Checklist

1. [ ] MAX_FORWARDING_SOURCES = 8 (max concurrent sources buffered)
2. [ ] MAX_PACKETS_PER_SOURCE = 2 (per-source packet limit)
3. [ ] Total buffer capacity = 16 packets max (8 * 2)
4. [ ] Send NACK upstream when per-source limit reached
5. [ ] Per-source limits enforce fairness (no single source monopolizes relay)

## Related Design Principles (from spec sections B.1, B.4-B.5):

6. [ ] Explicit backpressure: return ENOBUFS/QueueFull or NACK, never silent queue
7. [ ] No silent drops: signal congestion explicitly (NACK to mesh source if routable)

Note: No RFC 2119 MUST/SHALL/SHOULD keywords exist in this section. All requirements are implicit in the code snippets and descriptive text.
